body.x: The Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS), led by Minister Youngju Oh, operated the "K-Startup Pavilion" at CES 2025, which took place in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10. The pavilion supported 127 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in creating global market opportunities.

The K-Startup Pavilion, located at Eureka Park, CES’s startup exhibition zone, was created in collaboration with 30 startup-supporting organizations, including public institutions, local governments, universities, and major corporations. It showcased 127 startups, a significant increase from the 91 startups and 26 institutions last year.

The pavilion’s scale and the qualitative growth of its participating companies resulted in 12 Innovation Awards at CES 2025. AI solution provider NationA achieved double honors in the Metaverse category for the second consecutive year, contributing significantly to the pavilion’s 13 awards.

Sierra BASE, GhostPass, and Suprema AI were recognized with Best of Innovation Awards for their groundbreaking technologies in smart cities, fintech, and embedded technology, respectively. These achievements drew significant attention from global industry players, academics, and media even before the event began.

MSS's impact on Korea’s startup ecosystem extended beyond the K-Startup Pavilion. Among the 458 Innovation Awards announced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), 208 were awarded to 151 Korean companies, the highest number for any participating country. Of these, 127 were SMEs, with 86.6% receiving support through MSS initiatives such as R&D projects and venture capital investments.

KISED, established in 2009 as the nation’s only dedicated startup support agency, played a pivotal role in these accomplishments. Since 2020, KISED has facilitated the participation of 420 Korean startups at global exhibitions, helping them establish a presence in international markets and contribute to the worldwide startup ecosystem.

In 2022, KISED underwent a significant reorganization, establishing the Startup Korea Initiative to focus on globalizing Korea’s startup ecosystem. Debuting at CES 2025, the initiative actively supported the pavilion’s operations, collected feedback, and provided real-time solutions to participants. AVING News interviewed Changhyoung Lee, the initiative’s inaugural head, to discuss the journey of preparing the K-Startup Pavilion and plans for the future.

body.cap: Changhyoung Lee, Head of the Startup Korea Initiative at KISED, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. AVING News: CES 2025 marked the largest K-Startup Pavilion ever. What are your thoughts on its success, and how would you summarize the atmosphere at this year’s event?

A. Changhyoung Lee: Managing the pavilion, from planning to on-site operations, has been an intense but rewarding experience. The energetic atmosphere at Eureka Park has been invigorating and helped offset the exhaustion.

As the gathering point for global startups, Eureka Park feels more dynamic than other CES venues, such as the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC). I believe the K-Startup Pavilion significantly contributed to this energy.

The pavilion featured 127 startups, making it a standout presence. Approximately 1,300 startups participated in Eureka Park, with 650 from Korea, so our pavilion’s scale and impact were unparalleled. This achievement was possible thanks to the collaboration of over 30 public and private organizations. Overcoming challenges such as obtaining CTA approvals and preparing participants was no small feat, but our problem-solving approach proved effective. I’m proud of our efforts and deeply grateful to all the organizations and companies involved.
Q. AVING News: KISED is a leading institution driving innovation in Korea’s startup ecosystem. How does it plan to navigate the challenges posed by the current global economic downturn?

A. Changhyoung Lee: The government recently introduced the "Startup Korea" comprehensive strategy, focusing on supporting outbound ventures. This approach emphasizes helping startups refine their products and technologies to meet the demands of specific markets.

KISED acts as a coordinator, connecting companies with potential partners in target countries, simplifying local validation processes, and facilitating collaborations. The government views globalization as a key strategy for overcoming economic challenges, making 2025 the inaugural year of K-Startup’s "Global Voyage." Our startups, equipped with advanced technologies and strong potential, are ready to spread their wings on the global stage.
KISED will adopt a proactive and efficient approach to support these initiatives. Starting with CES 2025, we aim to lay a solid foundation for broader global success.

body.cap: Changhyoung Lee, Head of the Startup Korea Initiative at KISED, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. AVING News: The K-Startup Pavilion attracted significant attention. Could you highlight any standout companies?
A. Changhyoung Lee: The pavilion’s appeal lies in its scale and the exceptional quality of its participants. Many companies won Innovation Awards, showcasing their global competitiveness.

Sierra BASE, which received a Best of Innovation Award for its automated infrastructure inspection solution, exemplifies the synergy between KISED’s support and the company’s innovative capabilities. This recognition elevated the pavilion’s profile among global attendees.

Another notable participant is Greeneta, which developed the Keeep platform for creating high-quality 3D content. By drastically simplifying object creation and reducing data size while maintaining visual quality, Greeneta secured an MOU with NVIDIA.

Three companies won Best of Innovation Awards, and nine received Innovation Awards, achieving 13 honors. These accomplishments were made possible by leveraging insights and experiences accumulated over the years, creating a robust foundation for future pavilions.

body.cap: Changhyoung Lee, Head of the Startup Korea Initiative at KISED, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. AVING News: What are KISED’s plans for capitalizing on the achievements of the K-Startup Pavilion at CES 2025?

A. Changhyoung Lee: While data collection and evaluation are ongoing, the immediate results—such as contracts, MOUs, and investment deals—have been remarkable. We’ll continue supporting participating startups to ensure their CES experience translates into tangible value.

Upon returning to Korea, KISED will use its extensive expertise to solidify the outcomes of CES 2025. We also plan to share insights gained at CES through various programs and networking opportunities, inspiring other companies and institutions to pursue global expansion.
Our ultimate goal is to foster a virtuous cycle of input and output growth, elevating the K-Startup Pavilion’s standards and increasing the likelihood of participants achieving their objectives.
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
